Algebra I · Lesson 2.2

Evaluating in Practice

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Evaluating was settled in 1.6, so nothing about the method changes here, the expressions just get heavier. Substitute in parentheses, compute by the order of operations, read off one number. This lesson is six problems, and each one adds a step the last did not have.

Problem
Evaluate 5−4y5−4y at y=−7y=−7. There are two minus signs in the second term, one printed in the expression and one that comes with the value, so write the substitution with parentheses to keep them separate.
Show a hint
  • Read 4(−7)4(−7) as one finished product before subtracting anything.
Show the full solution
Substituting in parentheses gives 5−4(−7)5−4(−7). The product is 4(−7)=−284(−7)=−28, and subtracting −28−28 is adding 2828, so the value is 5+28=335+28=33​. Losing the value's sign turns the line into 5−28=−235−28=−23, which is exactly what the parentheses prevent.
Problem
Evaluate 3k4+20k43k​+k20​ at k=8k=8. The variable sits under a fraction bar this time, and it appears in two places at once. Enter the value as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Both kks become 88 at the same moment, one above a bar and one below, and each bar finishes as its own division.
Show the full solution
Substituting gives 3(8)4+20843(8)​+820​. Each bar finishes as its own division, 244=6424​=6 and 208=52820​=25​, so the value is 6+52=1726+25​=217​​. Combining across the bars into 24+204+84+824+20​ merges two separate divisions into one and is wrong.
Key idea
The same routine on harder expressions. Every problem here uses the routine from 1.6. Substitute in parentheses at every appearance, then work by the order from 1.2. What changes is where the variable appears. A letter can stand anywhere a number can, including under a fraction bar, and the bar still groups its whole top and its whole bottom. Write the intermediate values down so a sign error shows up on the line where it happens.
Problem
Evaluate −12w−12w​ at w=−3w=−3. The minus printed under the bar looks like the even-root trouble from 1.5. Substitute first, then decide whether the root exists.
Show a hint
  • Compute the number actually under the bar once ww is replaced, then judge.
Show the full solution
Substituting puts −12(−3)=36−12(−3)=36 under the bar, and 36=636​=6​. The minus printed in −12w−12w is not the sign of the value, so rejecting the root on sight would throw away a perfectly good number.
Key idea
Check the sign after substituting. An even root needs a nonnegative value under the radical, the rule from 1.5. The sign that decides this is the sign of the value after substituting, not the sign written in the expression. −12w−12w is written with a minus sign, yet it is positive whenever ww is negative. That is the point from 1.1. What a symbol looks like does not tell you its value. Compute the value under the radical first, then decide whether the root exists.
Problem
Evaluate n2−5n+3n2−5n+3 at n=−2n=−2. Three terms, three sign decisions, one value, and every appearance of nn gets its own parentheses.
Show a hint
  • Write the parentheses at both appearances of nn before doing any arithmetic.
  • Subtracting 5(−2)5(−2) is subtracting a negative.
Show the full solution
Substituting at both appearances gives (−2)2−5(−2)+3(−2)2−5(−2)+3. That is 4+10+3=174+10+3=17​. Two slips are common here, reading the square as −22=−4−22=−4, and dropping the sign in the middle term when −5(−2)−5(−2) is really +10+10.
Problem
Evaluate (2h−3)2+h(2h−3)2+h at h=6h=6. The parentheses hold a whole expression this time. Build the inside value first, square the result, then finish the sum.
Show a hint
  • The exponent applies to the whole parenthesized value, so finish 2h−32h−3 before squaring anything.
Show the full solution
Inside first, 2(6)−3=92(6)−3=9. Squaring gives 92=8192=81, and the total is 81+6=8781+6=87​. The exponent takes the finished inside value, so squaring term by term into 144−9+6=141144−9+6=141 is wrong.
Key idea
Inside out with variables. Evaluate a compound expression one piece at a time, innermost piece first. That is the inside-out rule from 1.2 applied to substituted values. In (2h−3)2+h(2h−3)2+h, the inside evaluated to 99. Squaring that 99 gave 8181, and the final sum uses that result. Each result is the input to the next step.
Problem
This one uses every skill from the lesson. Evaluate 1−12vvv1−12v​​ at v=−4v=−4. The bar covers all of 1−12v1−12v, the input is negative, and a division finishes the job. Enter the value as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Substitute before touching the root, so compute 1−12(−4)1−12(−4) under the bar first.
  • After taking the root, divide by vv itself. Its value is −4−4, sign included.
Show the full solution
Under the bar, 1−12(−4)=1+48=491−12(−4)=1+48=49, so the top is 49=749​=7. The bottom is v=−4v=−4, and 7÷(−4)=−747÷(−4)=−47​​. Two slips lurk here, stopping at the radical because of the printed minus, and dropping the denominator's sign to land on 7447​.
Fun fact
A GPS receiver finds your distance from each satellite by evaluating a compound expression, squared differences feeding a square root, inside out, many times every second.

The expressions got heavier and the method never changed. Parentheses on every substitution, signs judged after substituting, computation run from the inside out. Next, 2.3 turns the distributive property around, reading ab+acab+ac as a(b+c)a(b+c), a rewrite called factoring.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Evaluate 9−2t9−2t at t=−3t=−3.
Show the solution
Substituting gives 9−2(−3)9−2(−3). The product is −6−6, and subtracting −6−6 is adding 66, so the value is 9+6=159+6=15​. Without the parentheses the term reads 2⋅32⋅3 and the answer comes out 33.
Practice
Evaluate m3+m3m​+m at m=12m=12.
Show the solution
Only the first term sits over the bar, so it is 12÷3=412÷3=4, and the value is 4+12=164+12=16​. The bar groups only its own top, so pulling the lone mm underneath into 12+123312+12​ is wrong.
Practice
Evaluate 2−7d2−7d​ at d=−2d=−2. Substitute before judging the root.
Show the solution
Substituting gives −7(−2)=14−7(−2)=14, so the bar holds 2+14=162+14=16 and 16=416​=4​. What decides whether an even root exists is the sign of the value after substituting, not the sign printed in the expression.
Practice
Evaluate w2+3ww2+3w at w=−18w=−18.
Show the solution
Substituting gives (−18)2+3(−18)(−18)2+3(−18), which is 324−54=270324−54=270​. The square takes the whole value with its sign, so (−18)2=324(−18)2=324. Reading it as −182=−324−182=−324 drops the total to −378−378.
Practice
Evaluate (3g−4)2(3g−4)2 at g=5g=5.
Show the solution
Inside first, 3(5)−4=113(5)−4=11, and 112=121112=121​. The exponent applies to the finished parenthesized value, so squaring gg alone into 3(25)−4=713(25)−4=71 is wrong.
Practice
Evaluate 40p−pp40​−p at p=−5p=−5.
Show the solution
The first term is 40÷(−5)=−840÷(−5)=−8, and subtracting pp means subtracting −5−5, so the value is −8+5=−3−8+5=−3​. The divisor and the subtracted pp both keep their signs, and dropping either one lands you on 1313.
Practice
Evaluate h2+63h2+63​ at h=−1h=−1.
Show the solution
(−1)2=1(−1)2=1, so the bar holds 1+63=641+63=64, and 64=864​=8​. Reading the square as −12=−1−12=−1 leaves 6262 under the bar, which has no clean root, a good sign you took the sign wrong.
Practice
Evaluate a2+ba+ba+ba2+b​ at a=−3a=−3 and b=6b=6.
Show the solution
The top is (−3)2+6=15(−3)2+6=15 and the bottom is −3+6=3−3+6=3, so the value is 15÷3=515÷3=5​. Finish the whole top and the whole bottom before dividing, and remember a2a2 means (−3)2=9(−3)2=9, not −9−9.
Practice
Evaluate 2c2−c32c2−c3 at c=−3c=−3.
Show the solution
The even power clears the sign, so 2(−3)2=182(−3)2=18, and the odd power keeps it, so (−3)3=−27(−3)3=−27. Then 18−(−27)=18+27=4518−(−27)=18+27=45​. Treating the cube as +27+27 gives −9−9 instead.
Practice
Evaluate 50−t2t+12t+1250−t2​​ at t=−5t=−5. Enter the value as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
The bar holds 50−(−5)2=50−25=2550−(−5)2=50−25=25, so the top is 55. The bottom is −5+12=7−5+12=7, and the value is 5775​​. Both halves turn on signs, (−5)2(−5)2 is 2525 rather than −25−25, and the bottom is −5+12−5+12 rather than −5−12−5−12.
